g.text: A Boolean law is an equation between Boolean expressions
that holds for every assignment of values to its variables.
X OR (Y OR Z) = (X OR Y) OR Z
X OR Y = Y OR X
X AND (Y OR Z) = (X AND Y) OR (X AND Z)
X OR NOT X = 1, X AND NOT X = 0
X OR 0 = X, X AND 1 = X
Each law is checked the same way: run through
Every law here has a twin with AND and OR swapped.
Verify them yourself — the habit pays off later.
